feedback_request.integration_feedback: Report whether the signal is well behaved across the sensor span (is there a dead zone at the centre or saturation at the edges?), whether 5 sensors is more than needed, and whether any sensor is unused or redundant. Also say whether the sensor lookahead of 5 cm caused any lag or oscillation.

intent: Baseline balanced platform: five 12 mm sensors evenly spaced at 2 cm across ±4 cm, all 5 cm ahead of the axle, on a 12 cm track with 3 cm wheels. Aim is to complete all development tracks with few line losses and low lateral error, and to give the Integrator a linear, lookahead-based sensing layout to tune against.
learning: No prior race data. Next iteration, use the race telemetry (max_error and line_loss_events, in particular) to decide whether to widen the sensor span, move the sensors forward or back, or change the wheel track and mass for turn agility.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or integration feedback yet. I am starting from a balanced, mid-range platform. Five sensors span ±0.04 m across the 25 mm tape, so the line stays under at least one sensor through moderate lateral error and the reading-weighted signal is roughly linear in offset. The 12 mm footprint is about half the tape width, which gives a clear reading change as the line moves across it. The sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it, which should help at speed. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn rate and a top speed that can cover the course in under 3 s. Mass 0.8 kg with a 0.16 m body length keeps yaw inertia low enough to turn quickly. Body width 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at the 0.06 m floor, and a wider body would not raise it much. I expect this to complete the development tracks with a moderate line error. The next race should show whether sensor lookahead or track width is the limiting factor.
